finding.claim: Decrypted plaintext secret values are written to the logger at Trace level, violating the policy against logging sensitive data at any level.
finding.source: Any configuration value of the form {cipher}... from any provider (config server, env, files). Precondition: the value is an encrypted secret and Trace logging is enabled or reaches a log sink.
finding.sink: LogDecrypt(key, value, decryptedValue) -> LoggerMessage template 'Decrypted value '{CipherValue}' at key '{Key}' to '{PlainTextValue}'' (DecryptionConfigurationProvider.cs:58-59).

trace.note: CipherRegex().Match(value) detects the {cipher} prefix.
EnsureDecryptor builds the decryptor from ConfigurationRoot.
decryptor.Decrypt(cipher[, alias]) produces decryptedValue, which is the plaintext secret.
Only checks decryptedValue != value; no redaction.
LogDecrypt is called with decryptedValue as the PlainTextValue argument.
The Trace template logs the plaintext value.

finding.guards_checked: Log level is Trace (off by default), which limits exposure but does not satisfy the policy. No masking of PlainTextValue. The regex has a 1s timeout, which does not matter here.

finding.claim: A partial Vault client token (first 4 and last 4 characters) is logged at Debug on every renewal, and at Warning/Error on failure. Partial disclosure of a bearer credential violates the logging policy.
finding.sink: LogRenewingVaultToken(obscuredToken, ...) at line 846, plus LogVaultTokenRenewalStatus (851) and LogUnableToRenewVaultToken (856) at Warning/Error levels (templates at 1097-1104).

trace.note: RefreshVaultTokenAsync returns early if Token is empty.
obscuredToken = Token[..4] + '[*]' + Token[^4..]. Keeps 8 characters of the secret. Throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for tokens under 4 characters, outside the try block.
Debug log with the obscured token on every renewal cycle.
Warning log with the obscured token on non-200 responses.
Error log with the obscured token on any exception.

finding.guards_checked: Obscuring to 8 characters. Logging is Debug/Warning/Error, not Trace. The token is not logged in full. Still a partial secret in logs, which the policy prohibits.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated requests with arbitrary JWT 'kid' values trigger a synchronous outbound HTTP fetch of the authority's token_keys on each distinct kid. Negative cache entries are keyed by attacker-controlled kid with no size bound and no single-flight. This is an amplification and DoS vector against the IdP and the app's threads. Auth-path change: flagged for security review.
finding.source: The 'kid' header of an unverified Bearer JWT on any unauthenticated request to a JWT-protected endpoint.
finding.sink: httpClient.SendAsync(token_keys) at TokenKeyResolver.cs:124, invoked synchronously via FetchKeySet (line 111, GetAwaiter().GetResult() with CancellationToken.None). Cache growth at TokenKeyResolver.cs:79 and 68.

trace.note: IssuerSigningKeyResolver receives keyId from the token header, before signature verification.
Calls _tokenKeyResolver.ResolveSigningKey(options.Authority, keyId, options.Backchannel) with no pre-validation of keyId other than the resolver's null/whitespace check.
cacheKey = '{tokenKeysUri}:{keyId}'. Keyed by the attacker-controlled kid.
TryGetValue misses for each new kid.
FetchKeySet runs on every miss, with no per-IP or global rate limit or single-flight lock.
Negative caching only for the specific kid. Distinct kids bypass it, so each request triggers a new fetch.
Outbound HTTP GET per miss.

finding.guards_checked: tokenKeysUri is built from the configured authority, so this is not SSRF: the destination is fixed. Negative cache TTL is 30-60s but is per kid. The MemoryCache has no SizeLimit (lines 28-31). The OpenIdConnect TokenKeyResolver (src/Security/src/Authentication.OpenIdConnect/PostConfigureOpenIdConnectOptions.cs:72) appears to share the same logic and was not independently traced. Not dynamically tested.

finding.claim: The CF root actuator path is matched with an exact string comparison, so a trailing slash (or other non-exact form) skips the permission check and falls through to the hypermedia root without a token.
finding.source: HTTP request path '/cloudfoundryapplication/' (trailing slash) with no Authorization header.
finding.sink: Permission gate bypass: targetEndpointOptions stays null, so the RequiredPermissions check (line 89) is skipped, and the request reaches _next.

trace.note: Middleware is active only on CF platform with CF security enabled and the CF path prefix.
FindTargetEndpoint(context.Request.Path).
For CloudFoundryEndpointOptions only, the check is requestPath == endpointPath, which is exact. Other endpoints use StartsWithSegments.
A null target skips the GetPermissionsAsync and permission checks.
CanInvoke for the CF path checks IsCloudFoundryEnabled and HasCloudFoundrySecurity, not a token.

finding.guards_checked: Sub-endpoints (env, heapdump, etc.) use StartsWithSegments and are protected, so only the CF root is affected. The impact is limited to the hypermedia endpoint listing. I did not confirm the root's default RequiredPermissions or the exact rendered output.

finding.claim: The local root CA and intermediate CA private keys are written to disk unencrypted, in a shared directory above the app, and the leaf private key is written as plaintext PEM with default file permissions. A local user on the same host can read the CA key and mint certificates trusted by apps that use this CA.
finding.source: Local filesystem access by another user on the dev host. Trigger: running a non-CF app that calls AddAppInstanceIdentityCertificate.
finding.sink: File.WriteAllBytes(RootCaPfxPath, caCertificate.Export(X509ContentType.Pfx)) at line 62; intermediate at line 77; leaf key File.WriteAllText(...Key.pem, keyContents) at lines 99-100.

trace.note: Non-CF platform branch.
writer.Write(orgId, spaceId).
RootCaPfxPath is in ParentPath/GeneratedCertificates, shared across projects.
Root CA PFX written with no password argument and no UnixFileMode.
Leaf private key exported as unencrypted PEM.
Leaf key written with File.WriteAllText and default permissions.

finding.guards_checked: Writes only on non-CF platforms (dev scenario). Contrast src/Configuration/src/Abstractions/ConfigurationDictionaryMapper.cs:123-126, which uses UnixCreateMode user-only. The directory is created with default permissions. Permission mode and PFX password behavior were not verified at runtime.

finding.claim: Secret masking by key is suffix-anchored (`.*{key}$`) and the default key list lacks pwd/passwd and similar names, so secrets under keys such as 'Db:Pwd' or 'Redis:Password2' are exposed unmasked by /env.
finding.source: Configuration keys ending in a non-default or non-suffix secret word, with secret values present in the configuration.
finding.sink: Environment endpoint response: Sanitize returns the raw value when no matcher matches (Sanitizer.cs:45-58).

trace.note: Default KeysToSanitize: password, secret, key, token, vcap_services, .*credentials.*, .*connectionstring.* (no pwd/passwd).
Non-regex keys become `.*{key}$`, which requires the key to end with the word.
Key matching gates masking. Value-level masking (PasswordPairRegex, line 55) only applies to 'password=' or 'pwd=' pairs in values and does not catch 'Pwd' keys whose values are bare.
Sanitize is applied per property.

finding.guards_checked: Default key list and value-level regex masking. The env endpoint requires Full permissions on CF (EnvironmentEndpointOptions.cs:16), but on non-CF it is exposed by Include configuration. Behavior with custom KeysToSanitize was not tested.

finding.claim: The Redis connection string builder appends keyword and value without escaping ',' or '=', so a value containing ',' injects additional StackExchange.Redis options (for example allowAdmin=true, or changed sslHost/connect timeouts).
finding.source: Redis credential or setting values from service bindings or configuration (e.g. a password or custom setting containing ',allowAdmin=true').
finding.sink: ToConnectionString output passed to StackExchange.Redis ConfigurationOptions.Parse via ConnectionMultiplexer creation.

trace.note: Iterates non-host/port settings.
Appends ',' before each keyword.
Appends keyword unescaped.
Appends value unescaped. A ',' in the value starts a new option.

finding.guards_checked: No escaping or validation of values. RabbitMQConnectionStringBuilder.cs does escape (EscapeDataString / QueryString.Add), so this is inconsistent. Precondition is attacker control over one credential field, which often means the binding is already trusted, so impact is low. Not dynamically tested.
